operations.name: Charles Rothfiser

expected.charges: Federal prosecution under the Espionage Act of 1917 and/or the Sedition Act of 1918.
expected.sentence:
Twenty years in prison (Espionage/Sedition Act conviction).

ADMITTED TO BAIL, APRIL 2, 1919. The Federal Circuit Court of Appeals ordered thirty-eight of the men convicted in the Chicago mass trial released on bail pending its review of the case; the bonds ran from $5,000 to $10,000, with Haywood alone required to provide $15,000. Fifty-five others convicted in the same case did not seek bail. The order is not the release: each man left Leavenworth when his bond was actually furnished, which for those whose dates are recorded here fell between April 28 and September 28, 1919. Reported in the New York Times and across the wire services, April 3, 1919.

operations.name: LeRoy Nathaniel Bundy

expected.name: LeRoy Nathaniel Bundy
expected.description: LeRoy Nathaniel Bundy was a dentist and the principal Black political organizer in East St. Louis, Illinois at the time of the July 2, 1917 race massacre. The state authorities, declining to prosecute most white attackers, charged Bundy with conspiring to lead a Black "mob" that allegedly sparked the riot. Convicted March 28, 1919 in Waterloo, Illinois on testimony from Edward Wilson who himself admitted Bundy had not participated; sentenced to life imprisonment. Served one year, working as a dentist inside the prison, before the Illinois Supreme Court reversed his conviction (one juror declared insane; coercion of witnesses; insufficient evidence). Moved to Cleveland, earned law degree at Western Reserve, became prominent UNIA leader.
